_meta.description: Measured fixture geometry. footprint=[w,l] and height are the geom-AABB world extents; offset=[dx,dy] is the geom-AABB CENTER relative to the fixture body position (the value the renderer emits as <fixture>.position) — required because irregular fixtures (flat_stove) have collision geometry offset ~100 mm from their body origin, so an origin-centered clearance box misses part of the real fixture and a table distractor is injected penetrating it (RCA robot_distractor_settle.md). Missing offset defaults to [0,0]. top_z is the REST surface height above TABLE_Z (the distractor↔fixture contact surface, NOT max geom z). Generated by scripts/measure_spawn_clearances.py (measure_distractor_fixtures) + scripts/measure_fixture_offsets.py. settle_top_z (open-frame fixtures only) is the settle-measured height a FLAT distractor actually rests at on the fixture top — below top_z for open frames (rails) — used for the rule-2 analytic on-fixture DISTRACTOR z; absent ⇒ falls back to top_z. Generated by scripts/measure_spawn_clearances.py --distractor-settle-z. cradle (open-frame angled fixtures only, e.g. wine_rack): per-(distractor class) stable rest in the angled slot — dy=+y offset from fixture body toward the downslope, dz=body-center clearance above TABLE_SURFACE_Z, tilt_quat_wxyz=class-independent rest orientation, x_half=along-cradle x range. Measured by dropping each flat distractor into the cradle and settling and taking the median PRODUCTION 50-step settled pose across kitchen scenes (aligns the injected target with the realized settle, not the longer-settle limit); only flat-enough classes that seat without tumbling are listed (tall cubes fall back to table). The cradle block also covers FLAT-SEAT open-frame fixtures (wooden_two_layer_shelf): the shelf top is a real flat plate but the geom-AABB top_z sits ~80 mm above where a distractor actually rests (a flat object injected at top_z slowly sinks onto the plate over the long settle), so the naive top_z/settle_top_z analytic mis-injects and the fixture is flagged open-frame; the cradle rests store the measured per-class body-centre dz on the plate (dy=0, centred; tilt_quat_wxyz OMITTED ⇒ the distractor keeps its default upright orientation, no tilt), letting the fitting flat classes SEAT on the shelf top while oversized/ill-fitting classes (ketchup, macaroni_and_cheese, desk_caddy, bowl_drainer) fall back to the table. unstable_distractors (per fixture, optional): distractor classes that FIT the fixture footprint but cannot settle within pose-tolerance on its top (e.g. a tall class on the flat_stove burner GRATE tips/slides >5mm with a horizontal drift no spawn-z or rest-orientation removes, while settling cleanly on the flat table/cabinet) — they are excluded from that fixture and routed to the table, mirroring the cradle 'rests' seatability gate. Measured by scripts/measure_spawn_clearances.py --distractor-fixture-stability.
